chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a woman who emancipated a man, [the Imam was asked]: For whom is his guardianship, and for whom is his inheritance? He (peace be upon him) said: For the one who emancipated him, except if there happens to be an inheritor for him apart from her.
ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a slave emancipated by a woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'wilayah al-'itq' (guardianship of emancipation), establishing that a woman who frees a male slave retains both guardianship and inheritance rights unless a closer heir exists. It highlights the Shia juristic view that emancipation creates a kinship-like bond, prioritizing the emancipator's rights in the absence of competing heirs, thereby integrating manumission into the broader framework of Islamic inheritance law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazeyl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding a woman who emancipated a man. For whom is his guardianship, and for whom is his inheritance?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the one who emancipated him, except if there happens to be an inheritor for him apart from her’.
